title: Association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults: A cross-sectional analysis of CLHLS 2017-2018
content:
by Lunan Gao

Background

Prior studies have yielded inconsistent findings regarding the interplay between cognitive function, depression, self-care ability, and sleep quality in older adults, necessitating deeper exploration to elucidate these complex associations.

Objectives

This study aimed to examine whether self-care ability mediates the association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms, and whether sleep quality moderates this relationship in Chinese older adults.

Methods

We analyzed data from 7,580 older adults (aged ≥65 years) participating in a nationwide longitudinal survey in China (CLHLS, 2017−2018 wave). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10). Self-care ability was measured by physical activities of daily living (PADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL). Cognitive function was assessed using the Community Screening Instrument for Dementia (CSI-D). Sleep quality was measured using a single-item self-report question. Moderated mediation analysis was conducted using SPSS PROCESS Macro (Model 4 for mediation; Model 5 for moderated mediation).

Results

Self-care ability partially mediated the association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults (indirect effect β = −0.080, 95%CI [−0.114, −0.048]). Sleep quality moderated the direct path between cognitive function and depressive symptoms (β = −0.148, 95%CI[−0.245, −0.051], P < 0.05), such that the inverse association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms was more pronounced among older adults with poorer sleep quality. Of note, the pattern of mean depressive scores across sleep quality categories in descriptive analyses appeared counter-intuitive, which we address in the Discussion in light of the limitations of single-item sleep assessment.

Conclusion

Timely interventions aimed at improving self-care ability and sleep quality may be associated with a reduced risk of depression among the Chinese older adults. However, causal inferences cannot be drawn due to the cross-sectional design.
